A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MIRA and support comparison of the complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The missing detailed-results appendices in v7 are genuine removals, not extraction gaps.

before.justification: V5 reports original forecasting evaluations, missingness experiments, component ablations, inference timings, and expert-activation analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V7 retains original forecasting results, missingness experiments, ablations, inference timings, and expert-activation analyses in Tables 2–5 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: Appendix B replaces the reported iterative timestamp quantization, resolution refinement, and jitter procedure with per-sequence min–max normalization scaled by T−1. This changes input processing; the decoder, CT-RoPE attention, MoE, Neural ODE, and training losses otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: CinC 2019 is removed from the evaluation dataset description, Table 2, and Appendix G. The five pretraining datasets, other downstream datasets, and WHO FluNet missingness scenario are retained.

E2.justification: The baseline families and model variants remain the same in corresponding retained comparisons, including the general-domain and medically continued foundation models. Removing the CinC 2019 benchmark and detailed result breakdowns does not change comparator membership on retained benchmarks.

E3.justification: Appendix B reports different timestamp preprocessing for training and autoregressive inference: normalization replaces quantization and jitter. Stated holdout procedures, masking rates, model configurations, training budgets, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The WHO FluNet missing-rate experiment, component ablations, activated-expert sensitivity study, and activation visualization retain the same evidence in Tables 4–5 and Figure 3. The deleted appendix tables contain benchmark score breakdowns rather than separate robustness or ablation analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. Reporting point metrics averaged across forecast horizons remains unchanged.

E6.justification: V7 removes all per-horizon results in v5 Tables 8–12 and the CinC 2019 results. Table 2 also revises MIRA scores: large-model Heart Rate RMSE/MAE goes from 0.986/0.845 to 1.392/1.310 in the displayed scale, MIT-BIH MAE from 0.110 to 0.130, and ILI RMSE/MAE from 1.114/0.926 to 1.154/1.041. Small/base Heart Rate scores also change. Tables 3–5 retain their values. These are revised reported results; their relationship to the preprocessing change is unexplained.

T1.justification: Appendix B introduces an explicit mathematical definition of normalized timestamps in Equations 13–15, replacing the previous quantization description. The existing CT-RoPE derivations and Neural ODE assumptions, theorem, and mathematical arguments are retained after matching equation renumbering and the algorithm's relocation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same model, corpus, and benchmark contributions, including the 454-billion-point corpus and claimed average error reductions of 8% and 6%. These main claims are not recalibrated following the experimental reporting changes.

C2.justification: Appendix B shifts the processing rationale from avoiding timestamp collisions to stabilizing rotary phases, aligning training and inference time scales, and matching RoPE's index range while preserving continuous spacing. Interpretations of the experimental results and the deployment/privacy limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code link changes from HaoBytes/MIRA to microsoft/MIRA. Appendix B replaces quantization, jitter, and float32 instructions with normalization details. Deleting the detailed tables also removes dataset-specific forecast-horizon information. Hardware, epoch count, batch size, sequence length, and auxiliary-loss weight remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V7 removes the CinC 2019 sepsis-challenge reference by Reyna and colleagues, numbered 79 in v5. The remaining cited works, related-work discussion, model taxonomy, and research positioning are retained; subsequent reference renumbering is cosmetic.

P1.justification: Changes are concentrated in the rewritten and retitled Appendix B, shortened dataset heading, small code-label and footnote edits, and removal of Appendices J–K. The main narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V7 removes the entire set of detailed forecast-horizon displays, Tables 8–12. Table 2 loses the CinC 2019 row and changes winner highlighting. Table 3 moves from page 9 to page 8, corrects its caption to in-distribution, and simplifies group headings. Figures 1–3 are retained.

improvement.justification: V7 supplies an explicit normalization formula and corrects Table 3's caption and MIT-BIH RMSE highlighting. However, removing all per-horizon tables reduces auditability without reconciling their discrepancies with aggregate results. Table 2 also leaves MIRA-large's revised MIT-BIH MAE of 0.130 marked best despite medical-pretrained Chronos-large reporting 0.127. These reporting losses outweigh the limited corrections, while the core method and most aggregate evidence remain intact.
